answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small refundable stake before it can trade, and to earn trust only through verified completed work over time. Like a sparrow that must return to the same mesa nest again and again, an identity gains weight slowly, not instantly. A whisper of a new account carries no reputation, so an attacker spinning up thousands of fakes must fund each stake and do real costly work for each one, which makes mass fakery unprofitable while honest agents keep trading cheaply.
